title: Disable a system service from starting on boot
summary: Prevent a background service from automatically starting when you turn on your computer. This is useful if a service is causing issues or you don't need it running.
prerequisites: Know the name of the service you want to disable (e.g., bluetooth, cups, ssh).

steps.explain: Disable the specified service so it does not start automatically on boot.

placeholders.name: SERVICE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the systemd service unit to disable.

rollback.explain: Re-enable the service to allow it to start on boot again. This command is not on the current page, so consult the systemctl enable documentation or use a GUI tool if available.

warnings: Disabling critical system services (like networking or display managers) can make your system unusable. Only disable services you are sure you do not need.
